clue.text: Confront America in novel

parts.note: to brave something is to face up to it
the New World is the old name for the Americas

explanation.surface: A call to stand up to the United States, set inside a work of fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: Aldous Huxley's 1932 dystopia supplies the title.
explanation.definitionFit: Brave New World is the title of Aldous Huxley's famous dystopian book.

clue.text: Helpers in struggle to replace what's been used

indicators.note: things in a struggle are thrown about and wrestled into new positions

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Assistants battling to restock supplies that have run down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like part of the indicator but its letters belong to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To replenish is to refill or restock supplies that have been consumed.

clue.text: Chooses five books and even bits of verse

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books

indicators.note: the even bits are the second, fourth and so on, so only those positions in the word are kept

parts.note: second and fourth letters of the word

explanation.surface: Someone selecting five volumes plus some lines of poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: Votes as a verb means picks or elects, the same sense as chooses.

clue.text: Born eccentric, dry and boringly studious

parts.note: né is French for born, as in a man's former name

indicators.note: an eccentric thing is odd and off-centre, so the letters sit in an unusual order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A portrait of someone born odd, humourless and dull with study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' sits beside 'Born' to look like a character description, but it acts on 'dry'.
explanation.definitionFit: A nerd is a dull, obsessively studious person, so nerdy describes that bookish quality.

clue.text: Tornadoes, perhaps, twist above the streets

parts.note: to warp is to bend or twist out of shape
lanes are narrow roads

explanation.surface: Violent storms whirling over the city's roads.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'above' just places the first piece on top of the second. The Tornado is a combat aircraft flown by the RAF, not a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: The Panavia Tornado is a military jet, so tornadoes are an example of warplanes, signalled by 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Stood your ground, preferring to be outside

indicators.note: something ground has been crushed and broken up, so the letters are reformed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Holding firm in your position while longing for the open air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stood your ground' is a set phrase, which hides that 'ground' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An outdoorsy person enjoys open-air activities and would rather be out than indoors.

clue.text: Missing female plays pipes and string instruments

indicators.note: something missing is absent, so that letter is taken away from the longer word

parts.note: to flute is to play on a pipe
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A woman is absent from a band of pipers and string players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plays pipes' is a verb phrase: flutes, as in he flutes. Remove its F.
explanation.definitionFit: Lutes are plucked instruments with strings and a pear-shaped body.

clue.text: Tart's clientele showing dishonesty

parts.note: tart as an adjective means sour, sharp in taste
a doctor's or lawyer's practice is their body of clients

explanation.surface: A prostitute's customers revealing something underhand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tart' pushes towards a prostitute, but it is the adjective meaning sour.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharp practice is an idiom for dealing that is dishonest but barely legal.

clue.text: Famous sailor's mordant name for stretch of water

parts.note: great means eminent or celebrated
an old salt is an experienced sailor
lake is the name for a pigment fixed with a mordant

explanation.surface: A well-known seaman's sharp-tongued nickname for some body of water.
explanation.walkthrough: Mordant suggests biting wit, but a mordant is a dye fixer, and lake is the name of a pigment made with one; it also hints at the water's saltiness.
explanation.definitionFit: The Great Salt Lake in Utah is a large inland body of salty water.

clue.text: Cool dude from Perth is high!

indicators.note: someone high is drunk or intoxicated, and so are the letters, staggering into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A trendy man from the Australian or Scottish city is stoned.
explanation.definitionFit: A hipster is a follower of fashion who thinks himself cool.

clue.text: Spinner can turn it both ways

indicators.note: a word that reads the same whichever way you turn it is a palindrome

parts.note: the definition, a word for something that rotates, which also reads identically backwards

explanation.surface: A spinning top can rotate clockwise or anticlockwise.
explanation.walkthrough: The spinner turning both ways describes the word itself: spelt the same forwards and backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotator is a device or muscle that makes something spin about an axis.

clue.text: Equipment for catching river fish

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for river
eels are a kind of fish

explanation.surface: Gear an angler uses for landing freshwater fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as one description of tackle, but only the first three words define.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglers wind in their line on reels, which are part of the kit for catching fish.

clue.text: River finally emerges here, a branch of the Pacific

definitions.meaning: first meaning: where China's Yellow River ends up flowing out
second meaning: an arm of the ocean between China and Korea

explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' reads like a last-letter signal, but the first half is a cryptic hint at the Yellow River's outflow.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yellow Sea is a marginal sea of the western Pacific, fed by the Yellow River.

clue.text: Gestapo intelligence's secret location

indicators.note: a secret is kept concealed, so the answer lies tucked inside the words

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A Nazi spy service's undisclosed hideout.
explanation.definitionFit: A point is a particular place or position, a synonym of location.

clue.text: Artful tailor, son of a barber

indicators.note: artful means crafty or cunningly arranged, so the letters are cleverly rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A crafty clothes-maker whose son has a hairdresser for a father.
explanation.walkthrough: 'son of a barber' reads as family history, but 'of a barber' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonsorial is an adjective, from Latin tonsor, meaning relating to barbers or hairdressing.

clue.text: Guerrillas once protected holy man during clashes

indicators.note: to protect is to shield or surround, so one part sits enclosed by the other

parts.note: the Contras were Nicaraguan rebels of the 1980s
ST is short for saint

explanation.surface: Old rebels shielding a cleric amid fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: The holy man goes in just before the final S of the rebels.
explanation.definitionFit: Contrasts are striking differences between things, where they clash or jar.

clue.text: A letter and a card

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a written symbol such as one of the alphabet
second meaning: an eccentric or amusing person

explanation.walkthrough: Letter and card suggest the post, but a card is also a joker of a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Character means both a printed symbol and, informally, an odd or entertaining individual.

clue.text: Cousin Ted could be misleading

definitions.note: a noun here, the act of leading astray

indicators.note: could be says the letters might form something else once rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A relative called Ted may be deceiving people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misleading' looks like an adjective but works as a noun: leading someone astray.
explanation.definitionFit: Seduction is enticing someone astray, literally leading them away, so it fits mis-leading.

clue.text: Anna is worried about the people of Attica

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters surround the next word
someone worried is agitated and unsettled, so the letters are stirred up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman named Anna frets over the inhabitants of a Greek region.
explanation.walkthrough: Attica is the region of Greece around Athens.
explanation.definitionFit: Athens is the chief city of Attica, so its citizens are the Athenians.

clue.text: Call Doctor Doyle!

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with or falsify, so the letters are altered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone shouting for a physician named Doyle, or perhaps Dr Conan Doyle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor Doyle' reads as a title and name; 'Doctor' is the verb meaning tamper with.
explanation.definitionFit: A yodel is a warbling Alpine cry, a kind of call.

clue.text: Now prisoner's sacked brief

indicators.note: someone sacked is dismissed and removed, so those letters are thrown out of the word

parts.note: contemporary means of the present day
a con is a convict

explanation.surface: The current inmate has been fired from his short-term job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prisoner's sacked' means the prisoner is removed from the word for now.
explanation.definitionFit: Something temporary lasts only a short time, as does something brief.

clue.text: Chap supports me in fight

indicators.note: in a down entry whatever supports another word holds it up from below, so it is placed second

parts.note: taken as written
Lee is a man's name, standing for any fellow

explanation.surface: A man backs me up in a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, the chap supporting me sits underneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: A melee is a confused scuffle or brawl involving many people.

clue.text: Why Ike suddenly stifled an expression of alarm

indicators.note: something stifled is smothered and muffled, kept concealed within the surrounding words

parts.note: runs from the end of the first word to the start of the third

explanation.surface: Wondering why President Eisenhower abruptly held back a frightened cry.
explanation.walkthrough: Ike was the nickname of US President Dwight Eisenhower.
explanation.definitionFit: Yikes is an interjection people blurt out when shocked or frightened.

clue.text: Inhabitant's nearest pub

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a resident of a place
second meaning: the pub close to home that one regularly uses

explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as possessive, but it stands for 'is' joining two meanings. In Britain your local is the neighbourhood pub you frequent.
explanation.definitionFit: A local is a person who lives in an area, and also, informally, one's neighbourhood pub.

clue.text: Where scientists perform operations research work in US

parts.note: a laboratory, where experiments are done
OR is the standard abbreviation for operations research

explanation.surface: A place where researchers carry out procedures in their studies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perform operations' sounds like surgery, but the phrase splits after 'perform'.
explanation.definitionFit: Labor is the American spelling of labour, meaning toil or hard work.

clue.text: Peter is German musician

parts.note: peter is old slang for a prison cell
ist is the German word for is

explanation.surface: A man called Peter is a German player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peter' poses as a name; it is criminal slang for a cell (or a safe).
explanation.definitionFit: A cellist is a musician who plays the cello.

clue.text: Steadfast person in pursuit of UK retrospective for director

indicators.note: something in pursuit follows behind, so this part is placed after the other
retrospective means looking back, so these letters are read from the end

parts.note: taken as written
a brick is a reliable, loyal person

explanation.surface: A loyal figure chasing a British retrospective season for a film-maker.
explanation.walkthrough: A retrospective is also a career-spanning film season, apt for Stanley Kubrick.
explanation.definitionFit: Stanley Kubrick was the film director of 2001 and The Shining.

clue.text: Astronaut left Mars ingeniously preserved in liquid nitrogen

indicators.note: something preserved in a fluid is held inside it, so one group is placed within the other
done ingeniously means cleverly reworked, so the planet's letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for left

indicators.note: something liquid flows and has no fixed shape, so the element's letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A space traveller who quit Mars is frozen in liquid nitrogen.
explanation.walkthrough: Both the planet and the element are rearranged; L plus the shuffled planet goes inside the shuffled element.
explanation.definitionFit: Neil Armstrong was the American astronaut who first walked on the Moon in 1969.
